meta.title: Team Skills Matrix and Growth Planner
meta.note: The competency model is the ten demands from the 2026 Security Leadership Scorecard, so the matrix maps your team against what employers actually want. Ratings are your own judgment; this is a planning aid, not a performance review.

levels.label: Aware
levels.hint: Understands the basics; needs help to apply them.

levels.label: Working
levels.hint: Can do it with some guidance.

competencies.name: Framework fluency
competencies.blurb: NIST CSF, ISO 27001, SOC 2, and CIS, proven through audit.

competencies.name: AI security and governance
competencies.blurb: NIST AI RMF, OWASP LLM Top 10, and governance that enables AI adoption.

competencies.name: Cloud security
competencies.blurb: Hardening and identity across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.

competencies.name: Incident response and resilience
competencies.blurb: Owned, exercised response plans and calm command of a severity-one event.

competencies.name: Board-fluent risk communication
competencies.blurb: Translating technical risk into business impact for boards and auditors.

competencies.name: Industry regulation
competencies.blurb: HIPAA, GLBA, CMMC, GDPR, and the rest, owned through the exam.

competencies.name: Third-party risk and customer trust
competencies.blurb: Vendor risk inbound and security questionnaires outbound.

competencies.name: Automation and efficiency
competencies.blurb: Automating repetitive, high-volume security work to scale a lean team.

competencies.name: DevSecOps and the SDLC
competencies.blurb: Security embedded in CI/CD, IaC, and the paved-road developer path.

competencies.name: Player-coach leadership
competencies.blurb: Building, mentoring, and retaining a team while staying hands-on.
